items.caption:
This Sukkot, Chabad arranged a special day of visits for children to bring the joy and spirit of the holiday to seniors at the JCC Apartments, The Renoir, and Trinity Lodge.

The children and seniors quickly bonded as they played games, sang together, shook the lulav and etrog and enjoyed special performances by the kids. 🎶🌿

The children also baked delicious oatmeal raisin cookies especially for the seniors, adding a sweet treat to a wonderful afternoon! 🍪

There was so much laughter, singing, smiles, and connection throughout the day. 😊❤️

It was truly an amazing and uplifting experience, as the children brought happiness, warmth, and the joy of Sukkot to so many wonderful seniors in our community.

It is an ancient custom on Erev Yom Kippur (or the days in between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur) to perform Kaparot with a chicken, or alternatively with money. 
The value of the chicken or the money is given to Tzedaka and a prayer of atonement is recited.

Money collected from the Kaparot will benefit the families and individuals in our Calgary Community who are in need of assistance.

For additional details and instructions on how to perform this special Custom:

Visit Chabadalberta.org/Kaparot or hit the link in our bio! 

Gmar Chatima Tova to all! 🤍

items.caption:
Order Your Lulav & Esrog For Sukkot! Order Deadline: September 4, 2026

What is a Lulav and Etrog?

One of the special Sukkot mitzvot is the mitzvah of the "Four Kinds" - the lulav, etrog, myrtle and willow. This is a mitzvah like any other mitzvah of the Torah, but it is a very significant one and symbolic of unity and harmony. When the blessings are recited over them, it is customary to wave them to all the four winds and also upward and downward, signifying that G‑d is everywhere.

For Sukkah & Schach Orders:

Please email Rabbi Groner at jli@chabadalberta.org

Place Your Order at Chabadalberta.org/Lulav or hit the link in our bio!

items.caption:
It's been 365 days since the horrific terror attacks on Shemini Atzeret, which fell on October 7th. We remember those tortured, murdered and taken hostage. We remember the soldiers of the IDF who fell on, and since Oct. 7 fighting for the Jewish people. We stand strong with our brethren in Israel and worldwide as we pray for the return of the hostages and the safety and security of Jews in Israel and worldwide.

Live Jewish. Live Proud. For them.
Let's do a mitzvah today. May all their memories be for a blessing 🤍
